doubleClubSwingClean.name: Double-club swing clean to order
doubleClubSwingClean.purpose: Develop the bottom portion of a double-club swipe: coordinated hip-driven swings into a stable double order.
setup: Double-club work comes later than familiar single-arm and two-hand club work in this lesson. Use familiar manageable clubs with clear space outside the body.
Begin about 12–18 inches behind the clubs, feet generally forward. Reach down with thumbs pointing down, then rotate thumbs up and pack the shoulders.
steps: Hinge into the skiing-like bottom position. Let the clubs swing outside the body while the hips drive the movement.
Pull elbows inward and stop in a controlled double order, rather than a kettlebell rack.
Push, swing, pull and stop deliberately. At the bottom, keep straight arms in line with the body rather than reaching far behind it.
Set the clubs down with the same controlled technique used to pick them up.
bracing: The source describes lat engagement connecting shoulders to the back. It does not prescribe an exact breathing cadence.
The swing uses the traction-style ice-cream-cone grip; the stop compresses the upper hand with the finger/thumb OK grip.
mistakes: Wide elbows or elbows tracking behind the body: rebuild a stable, controlled order.
Treating the catch as a double kettlebell rack: review the different grip and order position.
Turning this coordination practice into a high-volume test: the source’s historical instructor test is context, not a prescription.
qualifications: The source describes this as back-burner coordinated skill practice after familiar swing, snatch or club work, with a couple of sets as an example. No automatic dose is implemented.
Swing clean precedes double pullovers and their later combination into swipes. These educational connections are not automatically measured technical qualifications.
Automatic training uses explicitly owned matched clubs and conservative app-defined practice doses; the source does not prescribe these exact numbers.

doubleClubPullover.purpose: Practice a controlled double-club overhead pullover back to double order after extensive familiar club preparation.
setup: This is a later, technically demanding exercise. Review familiar single/two-hand circles, shields, halos and gamma preparation before confirming the app prerequisite.
Set the feet under the shoulders, generally forward, then use a familiar double swing clean into order.
steps: Keep the glutes engaged and the pelvis controlled as both clubs move behind the head.
Minimize elbow flare, keep the elbows pointing forward and use the lats to return to a close double order.
Stay within controlled individual range. Stop if pelvic alignment, comfort or grip changes.
bracing: Maintain glute and lower-trunk engagement; do not dump the lower back when the clubs go behind you.
The source does not establish a mandatory breath cadence for every repetition.
mistakes: Letting the pelvis tip as the glutes relax: stop and review the earlier preparations.
Flared elbows or forcing range: reduce demand and return to familiar technique.

doubleClubTechnicalSwipe.purpose: Combine the double swing clean and pullover as a four-count technical swipe with deliberate stops.
setup: Confirm familiar component technique, extensive club preparation and current practice before combining.
Use clear space, a familiar matched pair and generally forward feet around shoulder width.
steps: Hinge and swing into order, then stop.
Perform the familiar pullover, return to order and stop.
Count swing, stop, pullover, stop as one complete technical repetition.
Keep controlled alignment and park the clubs with the same control as pickup.
bracing: The source describes a forced exhale at each technical count, allowing the inhale between exhales.
Maintain glute engagement through the top phase and controlled trunk alignment.
mistakes: Skipping the middle stops or losing wrist alignment: return to component practice.
Continuing with back pain or uncontrolled overhead range: stop and reassess; do not treat discomfort as progress.
